sources.title: Labor force participation rate for workers age 75 and older projected to be over 10 percent by 2026

sources.excerpt: The participation rate for workers age 65 to 74 is projected to be 30.2 percent in 2026, compared with 17.5 percent in 1996.

sources.title: Labor force participation rate for workers age 75 and older projected to be over 10 percent by 2026

sources.excerpt: For workers age 75 and older, the participation rate in 2026 is projected to be 10.8 percent, compared with 4.7 percent in 1996.

sources.excerpt: For workers ages 65 and older, the rate of part-time employment is even higher: 40 percent.

sources.title: Planning your Social Security claiming age

milestones.label: Living alone in later life
milestones.population: women counted in the Current Population Survey and reported in broad older age bands; the source publishes a living-alone share by sex for women only, and its oldest band is open ended, so the window stops where that band begins
whatChanges: A household of one becomes a common arrangement among the women counted in the older bands, and more common in the older band than in the younger one.
Tasks two people once split — bills, driving, cooking, checking that the other person got home safely — sit with one person.
Contact with neighbors, relatives and services carries weight it did not carry in a shared household.

milestones.label: Living in a residential care community
milestones.population: people living in residential care communities such as assisted living, counted in the national post-acute and long-term care study; the oldest published band is open ended
milestones.careNote: This is a count of where people were living, not a forecast for any one person, and questions about a particular person's care belong with that person, the people close to them, and a clinician.
whatChanges: Parts of daily life — meals, medicines, bathing, moving around a building — are handled by staff who are on site.
A household of one's own is exchanged for a room or apartment inside a community, with other residents nearby.
Relatives take on visiting, and often paperwork and money handled from a distance.

milestones.label: Written care instructions naming a decision maker
milestones.researchNote: Need a general-population study reporting the share of people who have completed an advance directive at a stated age or age band — a Health and Retirement Study analysis or a national survey of adults would do it. The NCHS long-term-care data brief cannot carry this: its comparison is an odds contrast between open bands inside a universe of people already receiving home health, nursing home or hospice care, which is a stock inside a narrow universe rather than an age at which anything happens.
milestones.windowInWords: Paperwork naming a decision maker and setting out care instructions, available across adult life with no starting age of its own, on file more often in the older bands than in the younger ones measured beside them
milestones.careNote: This describes paperwork some people already had on file, not advice about anyone in particular, and a clinician, or a lawyer where property is involved, is where a real decision belongs.

milestones.label: Hospice and palliative care, as services rather than events
milestones.researchNote: Need a verbatim eligibility sentence from medicare.gov or the CMS hospice benefit page, plus a use-by-age-band sentence from the CMS Hospice Monitoring Report published at cms.gov/files/document. Note that any age band in that report is measured among beneficiaries who died, which is a share inside a decedent universe and not an age at which anything happens.
milestones.windowInWords: A service that is available across later life with no starting age of its own, taken up by a share of people in the oldest bands rather than in a particular year
milestones.careNote: This only notes that a covered service exists and says nothing about any one person's situation; a clinician or care team is where that conversation belongs.

milestones.label: The span in which Social Security retirement benefits can first be claimed
milestones.population: workers insured for Social Security retirement benefits, under the claiming rules the agency applies; this is the span the rule permits, and no source here counts the ages at which people actually claim
whatChanges: A monthly payment begins, and the age it begins at sets the size of every payment that follows.
The monthly amount is higher the longer a person waits, up to the last age the rule counts.
Earnings and savings are weighed differently once a monthly check is arriving.

milestones.label: Withdrawals from a traditional individual retirement account stop being optional
milestones.population: owners of traditional individual retirement accounts, under the rule the tax agency applies; the same agency lets a person still working under a workplace plan wait longer, and that case is not what this age describes
whatChanges: A minimum amount has to come out of the account for that year, and again for each year after it.
The agency lets the first one be taken in that year or delayed to the first day of April in the following year.
Money that had been sitting untaxed inside the account becomes income in the year it is withdrawn.

milestones.label: Paid work continues for some people in the oldest working bands
milestones.population: people counted in the civilian labor force by age band; the participation rate is higher in the younger of the two oldest bands, and the oldest band the agency publishes is open ended, so the window stops where that band begins
whatChanges: Paid work carries on past the ages usually associated with leaving it, and part-time schedules are more common among the oldest workers than among younger ones.
Earnings sit alongside pension and benefit income rather than replacing it.
The oldest working band is the one the agency projects to rise rather than fall.

milestones.label: Reaching the oldest ages
milestones.population: people counted at the decennial census in the oldest age bands, including those who had reached one hundred years
whatChanges: The number of people counted at these ages has grown, while they remain a very small share of the whole population.
Most statistics stop resolving single years here and report one open band that holds everyone above it.
Services, forms and research designed around broad older bands rarely separate the people inside this one.
